metadata.remarks:
Network Third-Party Connectivity defines the capability to provide limited, bounded, and accountable network access for external entities such as vendors, partners, service providers, and affiliates. Third-party connectivity introduces elevated supply-chain and trust-transfer risk and therefore requires explicit boundary definition, continuous monitoring, and rapid revocation.

Governance and Responsibility Anchor:
This pattern is the authoritative anchor for SSPPs, standards, procedures, guidelines, and assurance related to third-party and external network connectivity. Controls are scoped to third-party sub‑capabilities to enable precise assessment of boundary enforcement and oversight.

components.title: Partner Connectivity
components.description: Establishment of network connectivity with trusted partner organizations under defined agreements.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Establish and manage external system connections under formal agreements.
Enforce boundary protection for partner network connections.

components.title: Vendor Access
components.description: Provisioning of network access for vendors and service providers for support or integration purposes.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Control and monitor external information system connections.
Authorize, restrict, and monitor remote vendor network access.

components.title: Responsibility Boundaries
components.description: Definition of responsibility, accountability, and trust boundaries between the institution and third parties.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Define and govern architecture for external network connections.
Establish policies governing third-party network access and responsibilities.

components.title: Monitoring and Revocation
components.description: Continuous monitoring of third-party activity and rapid revocation of access when required.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Monitor third-party network activity for misuse or compromise.
Disable or remove third-party access when no longer authorized.
